rule: FROZEN BEFORE click WAS BUILT. Written from the measured baseline in docs/BASELINE-CLICK.md, not from what the implementation turns out to do. Do not edit to match the build.
whatThePlaybookAlreadyHandles: scroll-into-view, covered, moving, disabled, iframes, trusted events — measured, and NOT re-implemented. click is an adapter, not a verb built from nothing.

criteria.must: a ref from read_page resolves to exactly the element read_page named — verified by its accessible name, not by position
a ref whose element left the DOM REFUSES. It must never act on a detached node, and never report success.
there is no way to pass force. Not a discouraged option — structurally absent, like headless. Measured: force:true on a covered button returns success and clicks nothing.
every refusal states WHICH reason — covered / not stable / disabled / gone / not found. An opaque timeout is not a report.
a covered element is REFUSED, never clicked through
click obeys the same sealed order as navigate: an element on an origin the order did not name is a HALT, not an error to retry
there is no submit verb and no form submission path, even when the last click is obviously harmless
the record carries role + accessible name + the ref, and NEVER coordinates
one call clicks at most one element. No retry loop, no fallback selector, no 'try the next match'.

acceptanceBar: C1-C9 all green as tests, PLUS a live headed probe against the frozen local hazard page showing covered/moving/disabled all REFUSED WITH A STATED REASON.
notAcceptance: A model-facing benchmark is NOT part of this. click takes a ref it is given; choosing the ref is read_page's job and was measured at 30/30. Adding a model to this loop would measure read_page again.
